sources.title: Topic no. 557, Additional tax on early distributions from traditional and Roth IRAs
sources.measures: the rule as written, for distributions from traditional and Roth IRAs
sources.excerpt: Generally, early distributions are those you receive from an IRA before reaching age 59½.

sources.title: Topic no. 558, Additional tax on early distributions from retirement plans other than IRAs
sources.measures: the rule as written, for distributions from qualified retirement plans other than IRAs
sources.excerpt: Generally, early distributions are those you receive from a qualified retirement plan or deferred annuity contract before reaching age 59½.

sources.title: Retirement topics - Catch-up contributions

sources.excerpt: Individuals who are age 50 or over at the end of the calendar year can make annual catch-up contributions.

milestones.label: Retirement withdrawals stop carrying the extra early tax
milestones.population: people holding traditional or Roth individual retirement arrangements, or qualified employer retirement plans, under the federal rule as written
whatChanges: Money taken out of an individual retirement arrangement is no longer treated by the tax code as an early distribution.
The same threshold applies to qualified employer retirement plans and deferred annuity contracts.
Ordinary income tax on the withdrawn amount is unaffected; only the additional early-distribution tax falls away.

milestones.label: Catch-up retirement contributions become available
milestones.population: individuals contributing to workplace retirement plans or individual retirement arrangements, under the federal rule as written
whatChanges: An extra annual contribution above the regular limit becomes permitted for those who reach the threshold by the end of the calendar year.
The allowance covers workplace salary deferrals and individual retirement arrangements, each with its own separate extra amount.
Whether a workplace plan offers the extra contribution depends on how that plan is written.

milestones.label: Withdrawals from an individual retirement arrangement become required
milestones.population: owners of individual retirement arrangements, under the federal rule as written for that kind of account
whatChanges: Withdrawals from a tax-deferred individual retirement arrangement shift from optional to required, on a yearly schedule set by the tax code rather than by the account owner.
The first required withdrawal is not due on the birthday itself; the deadline falls on the first day of April in the following calendar year.
A workplace retirement plan follows a different trigger: the requirement can wait until the account holder retires, where the plan allows that delay.

milestones.label: Extra health savings account contribution becomes available
milestones.population: individuals eligible to contribute to a health savings account, under the federal rule as written
whatChanges: The annual health savings account contribution limit rises by a set additional amount for those who reach the threshold by year end.
Spouses who each qualify hold the extra allowance separately, and each puts it into an account of their own.
Enrolling in Medicare ends the ability to contribute at all, whatever the account holder's age.

milestones.label: Federal age discrimination protections apply at work
milestones.population: applicants and employees covered by the federal Age Discrimination in Employment Act, as the statute is written
whatChanges: Federal law begins forbidding employment discrimination based on age against covered applicants and employees.
The protection reaches hiring, promotion, discharge, compensation, and other terms and conditions of employment.
It attaches automatically at the statutory threshold, without any application or filing.
